items.title: The closed-gradient resolvent is a genuine weak PDE solution

source.anchor: Appendix C.1 analytic Poincare prerequisite; background1310.2526v7 sections2.4-2.5
source.attribution: Samplinglib's explicit Euclidean weak-resolvent prerequisite to the analytic route for Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang; not a quoted theorem or full Lemma B.1.

items.statement: There exists u in the domain of the same closed gradient such that ε⟨u,v⟩L²(μ)+⟨G,D.closure v⟩L²(μ)=⟨f,v⟩L²(μ) for every domain test v, with G=D.closure u. The representatives u and G are locally volume-integrable and satisfy the ordinary weak gradient identity against every C1 compact scalar test and constant direction, including both integrable test products. For every smooth compact ψ, each of e^(−W)uψ, e^(−W)⟨G,∇ψ⟩ and e^(−W)fψ is volume-integrable and satisfies the displayed equation. This is εe^(−W)u−div(e^(−W)G)=e^(−W)f in the distributional sense, not a classical second-order equation.
assumptions: E is any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a Borel measurable structure, including dimension zero. W:E→R is C1, exp(-W) is volume-integrable, and μ is its normalized exponential tilt.

D is a given closable partial real-linear operator from scalar L²(μ) to vector L²(μ). Its graph is exactly the pairs represented μ-almost everywhere by (φ,∇φ) for smooth compact φ; WeightedGradient constructs such an operator.

ε is positive and f is an arbitrary scalar L²(μ) forcing. The theorem constructs one u in this same D.closure.domain and uses G=D.closure u everywhere. No weak equation, differentiability of u, or higher regularity is assumed.

The ordinary gradient identity uses all C1 compact tests and constant directions. The resolvent PDE uses smooth compact scalar tests ψ, embedded in the original gradient graph. Coercions select L2 representatives; all asserted integrabilities specify μ or volume.

formulae.label: Weighted weak equation
formulae.tex: \varepsilon\!\int e^{-W}u\psi\,dx+\int e^{-W}\langle G,\nabla\psi\rangle\,dx=\int e^{-W}f\psi\,dx,\qquad G=\overline D u.

obligations.label: Constructed weak solution, ordinary gradient and integrable weighted PDE tests

bindings.boundary: Weighted distributional PDE existence only. No H2, converse domain characterization, D*D operator core, Poincare, measurable fiberwise solution selection, or complete paper. Separately chosen resolvent witnesses are not definitionally identified.

assumption_deltas.source: Conditional Poincare is used in PBPS C.1; weighted Poisson/Sobolev arguments require actual weak solutions and admissible tests.
assumption_deltas.lean: C1 W, finite Gibbs normalization, same closable exact smooth gradient graph, positive epsilon, arbitrary L2 forcing.
assumption_deltas.reason: The closed-graph resolvent is constructed, and its PDE is derived by proving the test belongs to its domain; the desired equation is not assumed.

assumption_deltas.source: Actual PBPS conditional potentials are C2 with Hessian bounds.
assumption_deltas.lean: C1 W suffices for this weak prerequisite, with no curvature estimate.
assumption_deltas.reason: No quantitative Poincare or second-order regularity is claimed.

assumption_deltas.source: Background Poisson results on compact weighted manifolds carry regularity and boundary conditions.
assumption_deltas.lean: Weighted distributional PDE existence only. No H2, converse domain characterization, D*D operator core, Poincare, measurable fiberwise solution selection, or complete paper. Separately chosen resolvent witnesses are not definitionally identified.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is the direct full-space weak prerequisite, not the compact-manifold regularity theorem or a hidden transfer of it.

assumption_deltas.source: Use of density, representatives and integration in the analytic route is implicit.
assumption_deltas.lean: Same chosen resolvent witness throughout; C∞ compact domain tests; three weighted volume product integrabilities explicit.
assumption_deltas.reason: C1 inverse-weighted functions are not inserted into a smooth core. Separate chosen conditional solutions would need uniqueness to identify.
